headline: THE REPO NOW HAS A GATE THAT READS PIXELS, AND IT IMMEDIATELY CONFIRMED THE DEFECT LIST ADRIAN REPORTED FROM MEMORY. Every gate here was textual — check-contrast resolves the token graph in JS, check-hardcoded-spacing greps source, audit-tokens reads CSS text — so none of them can see a rendered box. That is not a gap in coverage, it is a blind spot: #245 shipped 55 structurally broken dark-mode aliases past every token gate, and the whole 'missing padding / smashed layouts / text breaking out of frames' class is invisible to all 58 existing gates by construction. scripts/check-rendered-geometry.mjs renders all 447 Storybook stories in Chromium and measures seven defect classes. FIRST RUN: 82 findings across 36 stories in 13 components, 0 render errors. Confirmed against screenshots, not just numbers: patterns-stacked-card-rail's first two cards are 168px and 203px holding 295px of content, so 'Token pipeline' and 'Component parity' run underneath the neighbouring card — Adrian's 'text breaking out of frames' is literally that. primitives-table's Token column is 240px against 258px of content, so semantic.color.content.primary collides with the Value column while Description sits behind a huge empty gutter — that is 'widths too small on some text' AND 'poor vertical alignment in the tables'. patterns-date-time-input has TWO controls rendering at 0x0, present in the DOM and unclickable, and its date field is missing the calendar icon its time sibling has — 'broken search icons'. primitives-breadcrumb's Home and Components are links with no underline and no border, so colour is their only affordance — 'links not underlined, states look noninteractive'. THE PROBE IS PROVEN NON-VACUOUS IN CI, not just by hand: 12 browser tests inject each defect and assert the matching detector fires, 4 assert silence on deliberate techniques (sr-only, inline link in prose, declared scroll container, rotating spinner). Mutation-verified — weakening MIN_TARGET from 24 to 0 turns the suite red. THE CANARY CAUGHT MY OWN BUG MID-BUILD: the first sr-only exclusion skipped anything 1x1, which silently swallowed the zero-size-control detector, the one that finds the broken icon buttons. A collapsed <button> is a defect; a collapsed <span class=sr-only> is a technique. The exclusion now keys on the clip declaration, not the size, and only applies to non-interactive nodes. Without that test the gate would have shipped quietly blind — the exact failure mode it exists to close.
next: THE GATE IS REGISTERED AS on-demand AND THAT IS HONEST — nothing runs it yet. It needs a built Storybook (pnpm build-storybook, ~2 min) so it cannot go in pre-commit. Wiring it to ci-pr is a .github/workflows edit, which IS pushable from a remote session (#267 proved it). Do NOT relabel the channel without wiring it: #276 found 30 gates recorded as firing that fired from nothing, and this would be the 31st.

82 FINDINGS ARE ACCEPTED IN docs/guardrails/rendered-geometry-baseline.json (57 fingerprints) SO THE GATE COULD LAND WITHOUT A REPO-WIDE FIX FIRST. The fingerprint is story + kind + selector and deliberately EXCLUDES magnitude, so a card that overflows by 127px and later 130px is the same unfixed defect, not a new one. Accepting a defect is therefore a reviewable diff, never a loosened threshold. Entries no longer observed are reported as fixed so the baseline gets tightened rather than rotting.

FIX ORDER BY BLAST RADIUS, all now measurable rather than argued: (1) primitives-table column widths — 10 findings across all 5 table stories, and Table is a primitive every pattern composes. (2) patterns-date-time-input — the 2 zero-size controls are the only unclickable elements in the whole system. (3) primitives-breadcrumb — 9 link-no-affordance, a WCAG 1.4.1 failure, not just a look. (4) patterns-stacked-card-rail — 13 overflow-x, but #133 may delete it, so confirm before spending.

32 small-target FINDINGS ARE A SYSTEM-WIDE QUESTION, NOT 32 BUGS: patterns-tokenizer (8), primitives-disclosure (6), primitives-slider (6), patterns-date-input (4). WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8 wants 24px. If the answer is a minimum hit-area on every interactive primitive, that is one token and one shared class, not 32 edits.

THE REMAINING SYNC AXES, measured: code<->Figma VARIABLES are in sync (drift 2). Code<->Figma COMPONENTS are 44 of 139. Code<->STORYBOOK is 113 story files on disk and 0 recorded in the manifest — the manifest cannot answer 'does this component have a story', so no gate can either.

56 STORIES ALREADY HAVE play() FUNCTIONS AND NOTHING RUNS THEM. @storybook/test-runner is config-only to wire and brings axe-per-story with it. It now shares infrastructure with this gate (a built Storybook + Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers), so the marginal cost has dropped.

A RED CI DOES NOT STOP A PUBLISH. .github/workflows/release.yml has no `needs:`, no `workflow_run` and no `if:` tying it to the CI workflow.

CHROMATIC CANNOT FAIL A PR EVEN ONCE ENABLED: .github/workflows/chromatic.yml:51 sets exitZeroOnChanges: true. As configured it is a report, not a gate — and check-rendered-geometry now covers part of what it was wanted for.

resolvedThisSession: PR #262 AND #261 ARE MERGED (c1561f5, 22ec2b5). Everything the previous revision of this file marked 'awaiting merge' is now on main: the 150 rewritten .d.ts specifiers and their gate, the registry channel relabel of 24 gates, and the three dead import.meta.env guards.

'use client' SHIPPED PER CHUNK, gated both directions (PR #268, open, green). scripts/lib/rsc-directive.mjs holds the rule so the build plugin and the standing gate cannot drift; check-rsc-directives re-derives it from dist/ rather than trusting the plugin ran. Canary: stripping the directive from dist/scroll.js makes the gate exit 1 naming that file. A spec review called the gate's import regex a confirmed LIVE bug; verified against real dist/ and the claim was wrong — Rollup renders import statements, esbuild only minifies chunk bodies, so imports always arrive spaced (11 scanned, 0 missing, 0 spurious). The fragility was real and was fixed anyway, tests first.

41 PROPS TYPES EXPORTED, gated from pretest (PR #269, open). The rule was written test-first and the tests earned it: the first pass read only an inline `export` modifier and silently missed three forms this codebase leans on — the trailing `export { CardHeader, ... }` in card.tsx, `Object.assign(GridInner, { Item: GridItem })`, and the one class component. Three tests for those went red before the rule grew; two guards (class STATE is not props; an inner component nothing re-exports stays private) went green FIRST, so the fix could not be satisfied by widening the net. Count went 35 -> 41. Canary: dropping `export` from AlertProps makes the gate exit 1 naming alert.tsx:61.

THE RELEASE DEADLOCK DIAGNOSED AND FIXED (PR #267, open, green). Not the org checkbox after all, or not only: GitHub's anti-recursion guard means no workflow run starts from a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored event, so PR #266 was born with zero checks. Option B (a PAT) was taken over an admin bypass deliberately, so the required checks keep meaning something.

A REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED WHILE BUILDING THE SECRETS WORK: the Supabase probe 404'd against the live ops project with PGRST125 because it appended /rest/v1/leads to a SUPABASE_URL that already carried /rest/v1 — the exact failure lib/supabase/server.mjs's own comment warns about. Fixed by reusing that sanitization, re-run clean against the live key, regression-tested.

RECORD-KEEPING CORRECTION, caught by the leak-proof sweep and verified: the previous revision of this file named scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs and scripts/check-published-types.mjs as present-tense fact. Neither exists on this branch or on main — both live in PR #262, unmerged. Every entry below now names the PR it depends on. A record file that asserts unmerged work as done is the same defect this session spent the day removing from the guardrail registry, committed in the one file whose job is to be true.

PUBLISHED TYPES FIX WRITTEN AND VERIFIED, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262 (nothing below is on main yet). 150 extensionless specifiers rewritten by scripts/add-dts-extensions.mjs; every entry point now green under node16 (from ESM) and bundler. Gated by scripts/check-published-types.mjs from smoke:consumer. Canary proven both directions: rebuilding dist/types without the fixer restores all 150 and the gate exits 1 with the diagnosis; running the fixer returns it to 0. attw profile is esm-only because there is no CJS build here and node10 cannot read exports, so both of those findings are design rather than regressions; the four CSS subpaths are excluded because a stylesheet has no types to resolve.

REGISTRY CHANNEL HONESTY, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262. The manual/pnpm-meta allowance removed from check-validator-wiring; 24 entries relabelled by the validator's own detection rather than by hand. Canary proven: setting check-source-canon back to manual makes the validator exit 1 naming the drift and fails exactly the three substantive assertions in the new test while the vacuity guard still passes.

THREE DEAD SHIPPED GUARDS, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #261. icon.tsx, deprecation.ts, TenantContext.tsx no longer read import.meta.env. Verified in dist/: zero import.meta.env, zero typeof process, the bare process.env.NODE_ENV member expression present. A first attempt guarded that read with typeof process, which a bundler leaves as a runtime check that a browser bundle always fails, inverting the answer in a production build; measured with esbuild and corrected before merge.

audit-gates-supportjson PROBE COHORT RESTORED, AWAITING MERGE OF PR #262. It selected its cohort with firingChannel !== 'pnpm-meta', so the relabel dropped it from 39 to 15. Now an explicit ID list seeded to match main, failing safe: a gate added tomorrow is included by default.

#236 CLOSED and figma/snapshot.json is on main (PR #258). Proven along the way that no agent can ever take it: the carrier runs fine through use_figma and returns a valid checksum (90bf34df), but use_figma truncates its response at 20 KB while the file is 255 KB — 12.8x — and --ingest checksums the exact bytes. A transport ceiling, not a credential problem. Two earlier failures were misread as transcription error before the runtime was shown to return function source verbatim and all ten functions to transmit byte-perfect; the guard was never at fault. The full DoD, the --json report and where each drift item is tracked are recorded in a closing comment on #236
